Then they asked Peter his brother

He, however, was unwilling,

And Maurice, when he heard, was afraid,
and fled and hid in Chalcedon.
Then the army, when it reached the royal city,
and Maurice was not found,
set up as king for themselves a certain vile old man whose name was Phocas.
And they went out and found Maurice,
and brought him to the city.
And they killed his sons before him,
and then they killed him too {OCR?}.
After Maurice, Phocas: eight years.
When Khosrow, king of the Persians, heard that Maurice and his sons were killed,
he put on black garments together with his nobles,
and made a house of weeping (mourning).
And while pretending that it was right to avenge the killers of his father-in-law and benefactor,
he made a pretext to gain dominion over the empire of the Romans.
And he prepared an army and sent it against Dara, and captured it.
And he entered Tur Abdin,
and for two years [besieged] Hisn Kayfa (Hesna de-Kefa) and took it,
and they killed the Romans who were in it.
And thus everywhere,
except for the Romans, they did not do harm.
Then the Romans who were in Mardin (Marda), when they heard,
abandoned the fortress and fled.
And the monks assembled and entered it,
and sent to Basil, bishop of Kfartutha,
whether he would permit them to kill the Persians.
And in the year 918
[918 of the Greeks,
607 of our Lord?], the rebellious fortress of Mardin was surrendered into the hands of the Persians,
and also Amida again.
And there was a harsh winter,
and the Euphrates froze.
And after two years the Persians crossed the Euphrates,
and captured Mabbugh, Qinnasrin, Aleppo (Beroea), and Antioch.
